reason: The image is a frontal (anteroposterior or posteroanterior) projection radiograph of the chest, showing the entire thoracic cavity including ribs, clavicles, spine, and lungs in a 2D superimposed view. A transverse section would display a cross-sectional slice (axial plane) typical of CT or MRI, which is not seen here.
case_description: A frontal chest X-ray displaying the thoracic skeleton, lung fields, and mediastinum. Visible medical devices include a right-sided port-a-cath, sternal wires indicating prior sternotomy, surgical clips in the left hemithorax, and external monitoring leads. The left lung shows significant opacity and volume loss.
